description: Wynem can be customised per server to fit right in with your server's theme. You can give Wynem a custom avatar, change the colour of its embeds, and change the prefix its commands use. All of these are set per server, so they never affect anyone else.

Wynem's avatar can be customised per server. The avatar is generated with the same Wynem logo generator as the [wynem](/commands/prefix/images/imagefun/wynem) command: pick your own colours, or provide an image to generate them from.

The avatar is always generated in the Wynem logo style, keeping Wynem recognisable no matter the server.
The logo is made up of four colours. Only the first one is needed, and any you leave out are generated from the colours you do provide:

rows: The vertical bar colour. Required, unless an image is provided
The horizontal bar colour. Defaults to the vertical bar colour mixed with white
The background colour. Defaults to a dark shade based on the vertical bar colour
The shadow colour behind the logo. Defaults to translucent black

description:
Colours can be any [CSS colour value](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color_value), like `red` or `#6C80F6`, and you can even provide a member to use their role colour.

If you provide an image, the vertical bar and background colours are extracted from it: the image's most common colour becomes the background, and its most distinct colour becomes the bars. The image itself is placed in the centre of the avatar, behind the logo.

tabs.name: Setting the avatar
content: To set the avatar, use the <command:wynemavatar [vertical-bars] [horizontal-bars] [background] [shadow] [image]|botconfig avatar vertical-bars:[colour] horizontal-bars:[colour] background:[colour] shadow:[colour] image-file:[image]> command. You need the **Manage Server** permission to use it, and the command has a `30` second cooldown.
For example: <command:wynemavatar #B81F23 #FE612C #431220|botconfig avatar vertical-bars:#B81F23 horizontal-bars:#FE612C background:#431220>

reply.name: Ewan
reply.message: e!wynemavatar #B81F23 #FE612C #431220used /botconfig avatar

data.title: Avatar set
data.description: Set Wynem's avatar for this server

content:
Wynem's avatar updates immediately, in this server only.

If you provide no vertical bar colour and no image (only possible with the slash command), the avatar cannot be generated:

author: Error
/assets/images/icons/error.webp
data.title: Missing colour or image
data.description: Provide at least the first colour, or an image to generate the colours from

tabs.name: Resetting the avatar
content: To reset the avatar back to the default, run the <command:wynemavatar|botconfig avatar> command with no options.

reply.name: Ewan
reply.message: e!wynemavatarused /botconfig avatar

data.title: Avatar reset
data.description: Set Wynem's avatar in this server back to the default

content: Wynem's avatar in this server is back to the default Wynem logo.

tabs.name: Rate limits
content: Discord limits how often a server avatar can be changed. If the avatar was changed too recently, you will get this error:

author: Error
/assets/images/icons/error.webp
data.title: Avatar changed too recently
data.description: Discord limits how often avatars can be changed. Try again in a few minutes.

content: Wait a few minutes and try again. If Discord rejects the avatar for any other reason, you will instead see a `Failed to update the avatar` error, and can try again later.

description: The embed colour is the coloured bar down the side of each message Wynem sends. It can be changed per server, and the colour can be any [CSS colour value](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color_value), just like the avatar colours.

tabs.name: Setting the embed colour
content: To change the embed colour, use the <command:embedcolour [colour]|botconfig embedcolour colour:[colour]> command. You need the **Manage Server** permission to use it.
For example: <command:embedcolour red|botconfig embedcolour colour:red>

reply.name: Ewan
reply.message: e!embedcolour redused /botconfig embedcolour

content: Every embed Wynem sends in the server, including the confirmation above, now uses the new colour.

tabs.name: Resetting the embed colour
content: To reset the embed colour, run the <command:embedcolour|botconfig embedcolour> command with no colour, or set the colour to `default`.

reply.name: Ewan
reply.message: e!embedcolourused /botconfig embedcolour

data.title: Embed colour set
data.description: Set the embed colour back to the default

content: The embed colour is back to the default Wynem colour.

description:
Wynem's default prefix is `e!`, but every server can set its own main prefix, along with up to `8` prefix aliases that work alongside it.

If you ever forget the prefix, just mention Wynem, and it will tell you every prefix that works in the server:

components.text:
## Wynem
My default prefix is `e!`, but in this server it is set to `w!`

Use `w!help` to view the commands that are available

Alternative prefixes you can use in this server: `;`

description: Custom prefixes can be up to 8 characters long, are stored in lowercase, cannot end in a letter or a number, and cannot contain spaces, backticks, quotes, backslashes, or the characters `|`, `<`, `*`, `~`, `@`.

tabs.name: Changing the prefix
content:
To change the main prefix, use the <command:prefix [prefix]|botconfig prefixes prefix prefix:[prefix]> command. You need the **Manage Server** permission to use it.

Provide no prefix to view the current one:

reply.name: Ewan
reply.message: e!prefixused /botconfig prefixes prefix

data.title: Current bot prefix
data.description:
The current prefix for <@Wynem> is `e!`

You can change the prefix with the command formatting `e!prefix [prefix]`

content: To change it, provide the new prefix. For example: <command:prefix w!|botconfig prefixes prefix prefix:w!>

reply.name: Ewan
reply.message: e!prefix w!used /botconfig prefixes prefix

content:
The main prefix has been replaced, so commands now use `w!` instead of `e!`.

To return to the default prefix, set the prefix to `default`, `normal`, or `reset`:

reply.name: Ewan
reply.message: w!prefix resetused /botconfig prefixes prefix

content: If the prefix does not follow the prefix rules, it will be rejected:

author: Error
/assets/images/icons/error.webp
data.title: Invalid prefix
data.description: Custom prefixes cannot end in a letter or a number

tabs.name: Prefix aliases
content:
A prefix alias is an alternate prefix that can be used without overwriting the main prefix. A server can have up to `8` prefix aliases, and they follow the same rules as the main prefix.

To add one, use the <command:prefixalias [prefix]|botconfig prefixes prefixalias prefix:[prefix]> command. You need the **Manage Server** permission to use it.
For example: <command:prefixalias ;|botconfig prefixes prefixalias prefix:;>

reply.name: Ewan
reply.message: e!prefixalias ;used /botconfig prefixes prefixalias

data.title: Custom prefix alias added
data.description: You can now use `;` as an alternative prefix

content: Running the same command again with the same prefix removes the alias:

reply.name: Ewan
reply.message: e!prefixalias ;used /botconfig prefixes prefixalias

data.title: Custom prefix alias removed
data.description: The prefix `;` is no longer a custom prefix alias

content: Provide no prefix to view the current aliases:

reply.name: Ewan
reply.message: e!prefixaliasused /botconfig prefixes prefixalias

data.title: Custom prefix aliases
data.description:
`w!`, `;`

You can add more custom prefix aliases with the `e!prefixalias [prefix]` command

content: An alias cannot be the default prefix or the server's current main custom prefix. If you want to use the default prefix while a custom main prefix is set, Wynem will suggest the fix:

author: Error
/assets/images/icons/error.webp
data.title: Unable to add prefix alias
data.description:
That is <@Wynem>'s default prefix

If you want to use this prefix, set the server prefix back to default and then use an alias prefix instead of a main one

tabs.name: Prefixless mode
content:
In direct messages with Wynem, you can skip prefixes entirely. Prefixless mode is a personal toggle that only applies to your own DMs with Wynem, and the `prefixlessmode` command can only be used there.

To toggle it, send `e!prefixlessmode` to Wynem in a direct message:

data.title: Prefixless mode enabled
data.description: Commands in direct messages no longer require a prefix

content: You can now use commands in Wynem's DMs without any prefix, like `help` instead of `e!help`. Run the command again to turn it back off:

data.title: Prefixless mode disabled
data.description: Commands in direct messages now require the prefix `e!`
